_what_this_is: The batch manifest. CHAT WRITES THE IDS AND THEY ARE IMMUTABLE; the agent may only move `status` and add `evidence`. `id_lock` is a hash over the ordered id list and `batch_manifest.py --check` refuses a manifest whose ids have been renumbered, duplicated, added to or removed.

DONE, landed as `953d70a3` -- docs/cloud-research/2026-10-20-eu-law-route-and-the-three-audits-eu-limbs.md. THE ROUTE IS FIXED AND IT IS THE OFFICIAL MACHINE INTERFACE, NOT A WORKAROUND: the EU Publications Office exposes CELLAR with HTTP content negotiation on a CELEX identifier -- GET http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX> with Accept: application/xhtml+xml. AI Act 32024R1689 -> HTTP 200, 1,257,134 bytes; AMLR 32024R1624 -> HTTP 200, 1,165,026 bytes; both 303 to a Cellar resource, which is the documented behaviour of the identifier service. No bot wall is involved and none is circumvented -- the same rule as b38/b39 applied to eCFR: stop at the wall, find the published machine interface. Re-runnable: scratchpad/b40/eu_fetch.py. THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE AI ACT IS NOT A FUTURE CLIFF -- Article 113 read from source: applies from 2 AUGUST 2026, Chapters I and II from 2 February 2025, Chapter III Section 4 / V / VII / XII and Article 78 from 2 August 2025, and ARTICLE 6(1) from 2 AUGUST 2027. Today is 2026-10-20, so the general application date is ELEVEN WEEKS PAST and all three prior audits treated it as ahead. AND THE ANSWER FOR SAIRNCODE IS A NEGATIVE ONE ON THE ACTOR TEST: Annex III 5(a) is 'by public authorities or on behalf of public authorities', 5(c) is pricing for life and health insurance (the INSURER's side), 5(d) is emergency triage, and 6(1) needs an Annex I product under third-party conformity assessment -- so SAIRNcode is NOT Annex III high-risk, stated as a BOUNDARY rather than a clearance because a sale to a payer or public authority would engage 5(a) or 5(c) without any code change. AMLR Article 90 confirms b37's dates FROM SOURCE: 10 July 2027, except Article 3(3)(n) and (o) at 10 July 2029 -- b37 was right from a snippet and b38/b39 refused to cite it. AND THE PRIVILEGE CARVE-OUT HAS A CLAUSE NO AUDIT HAD: it covers information received 'before, during or after' proceedings, and the exception ends 'Such knowledge and purpose can be inferred from objective factual circumstances' -- so the carve-out is NOT SELF-CERTIFYING and the record the software keeps is part of those circumstances, which makes b38's AML decision harder to defer, not easier.
